content.problemStatement: Users report that generated short codes (7 base62 characters) feel guessable. Raise the entropy of newly generated codes to 8 base62 characters (62^8 ≈ 2.2e14 keys) without changing anything about codes that have already been issued: legacy 7-character codes and all custom aliases must keep resolving.

functionalRequirements.text: Newly generated codes are 8 base62 characters by default (configurable via shortener.code-length).
All previously issued codes (7-char generated, custom aliases of any accepted length) keep resolving on GET /:code, metadata and stats.

nonFunctionalRequirements.text: No measurable latency change on redirect.
Backward compatible API for existing clients.

acceptanceCriteria.given: a legacy 7-char code exists in the store

assumptions: 'Guess' refers to an attacker or curious user finding links they were not given.
No incident has occurred; this is preventive hardening.
outOfScope: Authentication for viewing links (unless AMB-1 selects C)

ambiguities.question: What does 'too easy to guess' mean for the users who complained?

options.description: Generated codes are short (7 base62 chars); raise their entropy (e.g. 8 chars, 62^8 ≈ 2.2e14).
options.impact: Small, contained change to config/codegen and tests; legacy 7-char codes keep resolving.

options.description: User-chosen custom aliases are predictable ('sale1', 'promo2'); enforce alias rules (minimum length, maybe a denylist).
options.impact: Validation change in the domain model and routes; must not break already-issued short aliases.

options.description: Users expect links to be private; add unlisted/authenticated links.
options.impact: A new feature (tokens or auth), not a hardening change; separate product decision.

ambiguities.resolution: Stakeholder chose A: the tickets concern generated codes. Raise generated code length to 8.

ambiguities.question: Should already-issued codes be regenerated to the new rule?

options.description: Only new links follow the new rule
options.impact: Zero breakage; old links stay as guessable as they were.
Breaks every link already shared; unacceptable.

risks.risk: Building the wrong interpretation wastes an implementation cycle.
Tightening any pattern used by the routes breaks legacy codes.
risks.mitigation: Separate creation-time rules from path-resolution rules; acceptance test for legacy codes.
